paragraphs.title: Crying Out to God and Asking Him to Listen

easy.explanation: He says, “Unto thee will I cry, O LORD my rock.”
easy.q: To whom does the worshiper cry?
What does the worshiper call the LORD?

easy.explanation: He asks, “be not silent to me.”
easy.q: What does the worshiper ask the LORD not to do?

medium.explanation: He cries unto the LORD and lifts up his hands toward God’s holy oracle.
medium.q: What does the worshiper do while crying unto the LORD?

answers: A holy place connected with God’s presence
medium.explanation: The worshiper raises his hands toward the LORD’s holy sanctuary.
medium.q: What does “holy oracle” refer to in this passage?

answers: He fears becoming like those who go down into the pit
He wants to defeat the people
medium.explanation: He says that if the LORD is silent, he may become like them that go down into the pit.
medium.q: Why does the worshiper ask the LORD not to be silent?

answers: Both are expressions of prayer and appeal
Both express anger against the people
challenge.explanation: The verses present crying and lifting up the hands as ways of seeking God.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between crying and lifting up the hands?

answers: He will become like those who go down into the pit
challenge.explanation: He fears becoming like “them that go down into the pit.”
challenge.q: What may happen if the LORD does not answer the worshiper?

answers: The LORD is his firm source of strength and security
The LORD is one of the wicked
The LORD does not hear prayer
challenge.explanation: Calling the LORD his rock expresses trust in Him as a secure refuge.
challenge.q: What does the title “my rock” suggest about the worshiper’s relationship with the LORD?

paragraphs.title: Separation from the Wicked and Their Retribution

answers: The wicked and workers of iniquity
easy.explanation: He asks, “Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity.”
easy.q: With whom does the worshiper ask not to be drawn away?

easy.explanation: They are described as those “which speak peace to their neighbours.”
easy.q: What do these people speak to their neighbours?

easy.explanation: Although they speak peace, “mischief is in their hearts.”

answers: The recompense or result they deserve
medium.explanation: “Their desert” means what they deserve because of their actions.
medium.q: What does “their desert” mean in this passage?

answers: Their deeds and the work of their hands
medium.explanation: He asks God to give them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.
medium.q: According to what does the worshiper ask that they be repaid?

answers: They do not regard the works of the LORD
medium.explanation: They do not regard the works of the LORD or the operation of His hands.
medium.q: Why does the worshiper ask for this judgment?

answers: They speak peace but keep mischief in their hearts
They remain silent but sing to the LORD
They pray while asking for blessing
challenge.explanation: Their peaceful words conceal the mischief in their hearts.
challenge.q: What is the main contradiction in the behavior of these people?

answers: God will destroy them and not build them up
Their ignorance will bring them blessing
challenge.explanation: Because they do not regard God’s works, “he shall destroy them, and not build them up.”
challenge.q: What connection do the verses make between ignoring God’s works and the wicked’s fate?

answers: Their recompense corresponds to their actions
They are concerned only with building
They are connected with the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that their judgment is related to what they have done.
challenge.q: What does the repeated reference to deeds and the work of their hands emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving for Help and Trust in God

answers: Because He has heard his supplications
Because He built him a city
easy.explanation: He blesses the LORD because He has heard the voice of his supplications.
easy.q: Why does the worshiper bless the LORD?

easy.explanation: The worshiper says, “The LORD is my strength and my shield.”
easy.q: What is the LORD to the worshiper?

easy.explanation: He says, “therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth.”
easy.q: How does the worshiper’s heart respond?

answers: The sound of his requests and prayers
medium.explanation: Supplications are humble requests or prayers.
medium.q: What does “the voice of my supplications” mean?

answers: His trust in the LORD and the help he received
The peaceful words of the wicked
medium.explanation: He trusted in the LORD and was helped, so his heart rejoiced.
medium.q: What caused the worshiper’s heart to rejoice?

medium.explanation: He says, “with my song will I praise him.”
medium.q: How does the worshiper express his thanks?

challenge.explanation: The worshiper moves from prayer to God’s hearing and help, followed by praise.
challenge.q: What order of thought appears in these verses?

answers: Trust brings help and leads to a song of praise
Trust causes a person to join the wicked
challenge.explanation: He trusted in the LORD, was helped, rejoiced, and praised Him in song.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between trusting the LORD and praising Him?

answers: He prevents the worshiper from rejoicing
challenge.explanation: A shield represents protection, and the LORD is described as the worshiper’s protector.
challenge.q: What does the image of a “shield” emphasize about the LORD?

paragraphs.title: Prayer for the People and Their King

answers: The strength of the wicked only
Those who go down into the pit
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD is their strength.”
easy.q: What is the LORD to His people?
Whom does the worshiper ask the LORD to save?
What does the worshiper ask the LORD to do to His inheritance?

answers: The people belonging to the LORD
The dwelling place of the wicked
medium.explanation: The inheritance refers to the people claimed by and belonging to the LORD.
medium.q: What does “thine inheritance” refer to in this context?

answers: As a shepherd feeds and lifts up a flock
medium.explanation: He asks the LORD to “feed them also, and lift them up.”
medium.q: How does the worshiper ask the LORD to care for His people?

medium.explanation: The prayer ends with the words “for ever.”
medium.q: How long does the worshiper ask the LORD to lift up His people?

answers: The prayer moves from personal need to the people and their king
The prayer moves from the people to a description of the wicked
The prayer changes from thanksgiving to a private request only
challenge.explanation: The closing verses expand the prayer to include the people and the LORD’s anointed.
challenge.q: What change takes place at the end of the psalm?

answers: The LORD is the source of salvation and strength for His chosen king
The anointed one is a place where the wicked live
Salvation is unrelated to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The LORD is described as the saving strength of His anointed.
challenge.q: What does “the saving strength of his anointed” communicate?

answers: Blessing, shepherding, lifting up, and lasting care
challenge.explanation: The worshiper asks the LORD to save, bless, feed, and lift up His people forever.
challenge.q: What does the final request include besides salvation?
